title: Liverpool Edge Chelsea in the Camara Race, but the Back Line Is the Real Story
body:
Liverpool are reportedly ahead of Chelsea in the race for Monaco's Lamine Camara [S1]. The same round-up says Barcelona have closed the door on moves for Virgil van Dijk and Bruno Fernandes [S1], and that Wilfried Zaha, once of Palace, could come back to the club [S1]. On Van Dijk, BBC Sport frames the situation as a decision that Liverpool and the defender still have to make [S2]. He has said he is not panicking about his contract [S2].

The form guide adds some context. Liverpool's last five league matches brought three wins, two defeats and nine points, with seven goals scored and six conceded [ST1]. Chelsea have the same three wins, two defeats and nine points, but they have scored nine and conceded only four [ST2].

On paper the two sides look level in the table, but the difference sits at the back. A team shipping goals at that rate has a clear problem, and goals conceded are harder to hide than a rumour. Any ambitious side needs a settled defence more than a headline signing, so the transfer chatter should be judged on whether it actually fixes that.

Talk is cheap until the paperwork is signed. If a deal does go through, it will say plenty about where the club believes it is heading, and that is the story worth watching.

The Touchline Take: judge the business when the window shuts, not before.
